articles.title: Night: Ambush Green
articles.summary: Deep forest green with a fine even sparkle, flat and shadowless, like leaves lit from everywhere at once. Reads as a deep forest green with a lively grain; the speckle averages out to a dark matte-ish green, not a camo print.

Up close: Very fine speckle of dark forest green and mid green with scattered pale-mint pixels, 2-6px grains with no shapes, edges or direction; like moss, or foliage seen so close every leaf blends in. A slightly darker cloud drifts across it. From a distance: Reads as a deep forest green with a lively grain; the speckle averages out to a dark matte-ish green, not a camo print. Measured spec (average): metal 104, roughness 122, coat 192. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.

articles.title: Field: Canvas Duck
articles.summary: Woven tan cotton grid, like a waxed canvas tarp laid flat; dull khaki with faint vertical ribbing. Reads as a muted khaki-brown with widely spaced light pinstripes running up and down; the thread grid is just a fine grain.
articles.what: Twelve-ounce cotton, waxed, that stands up on its own after a season. Up close: Khaki-tan fabric with a fine square weave grid of 3-4 px threads, crossed by pale cream vertical ribs about 40 px apart that lean slightly off-vertical, and faint white fibre scratches scattered over it. Looks like waxed canvas or ripstop tarp. From a distance: Reads as a muted khaki-brown with widely spaced light pinstripes running up and down; the thread grid is just a fine grain. Measured spec (average): metal 7, roughness 105, coat 94. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Field: Canvas Duck" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Roof, hood and sides: wide panels show the ribs
Pair with a dark rocker band and olive or black numbers
Mid-busy: black, olive or white numbers with an outline read; khaki or brown numbers disappear.
Stencil lettering or army-style markings: field-gear story
Pairs well with: olive drab, burnt orange, black, cream.
pitfalls: Not burlap or hessian: threads are tight and even with sharp ribs
Not plaid or gingham: one colour, just vertical light ribs
Avoid: small numbers over the weave, next to glossy tech finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 7 (non-metal paint), roughness 105 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 94 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the weave, next to glossy tech finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: stencil lettering or army-style markings: field-gear story; wide olive or black stripes: structure and number area
Patterns to avoid: other weaves or carbon: moire with the thread grid; glossy tech patterns: wrong mood
Spec overlays that work: matte clearcoat dulling: waxed canvas look; rough grit: more fabric tooth
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Hardware: Carbon Handguard
articles.summary: Dark charcoal twill-weave carbon under gloss resin, faint diagonal check pattern, bright sheen on curves. A dark charcoal-grey with a fine sparkly mesh shimmer; individual dots blur into a techy graphite grain with a glossy sheen.
articles.what: Twill weave under resin, cool to the touch after a string nobody should fire. Up close: A tight, regular lattice of small bright dots on charcoal, a few pixels apart, each dot a woven-tow crossing; light and dark cells alternate in a checker rhythm and the grid wobbles slightly. Reads as fine twill carbon under resin, not a smooth sheet. From a distance: A dark charcoal-grey with a fine sparkly mesh shimmer; individual dots blur into a techy graphite grain with a glossy sheen. Measured spec (average): metal 15, roughness 32, coat 30. Shine: high gloss. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Hardware: Carbon Handguard" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, splitter and mirrors: classic carbon spots with broad flat area to show weave
Avoid tiny trim: weave is too fine to read
White, red or neon numbers pop cleanly; very dark numbers disappear into the charcoal weave.
Thin pinstripes or stripe graphics: sit cleanly on the fine weave
Pairs well with: red, white, chrome, neon green.
pitfalls: Not forged carbon: the weave is a regular grid, not chopped random shards
Not a metallic flake: the glints are weave crowns, metal is none
Avoid: busy patterns over the weave hide it, very dark numbers on it.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 15 (non-metal paint), roughness 32 (high gloss), clearcoat 30 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: busy patterns over the weave hide it, very dark numbers on it.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: thin pinstripes or stripe graphics: sit cleanly on the fine weave; large flat decals/camo blocks: weave stays as a quiet bed underneath
Patterns to avoid: busy fine patterns (hex, static, dots): fight the weave and mush
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat boost: deepens the resin look; subtle micro-flake: adds a wet sparkle without hiding the weave
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Field: Cedar Decoy
articles.summary: Fine, even earthy brown grain with a semi-matte finish and a faint sparkle across the surface. Reads as a dull earthy bronze-brown with a dirty, sandy feel; the speckle collapses into a flat olive-tan to mid-brown colour with slight mottling.
articles.what: Carved, painted, and chipped by forty seasons of being thrown into a bag. Up close: Very fine two-tone speckle: tan-gold grains over a dark brown-black ground, with irregular tiny pits and holes 2-5 px across, like chipped paint worn through to dark wood. Soft darker and lighter cloud patches roll underneath. From a distance: Reads as a dull earthy bronze-brown with a dirty, sandy feel; the speckle collapses into a flat olive-tan to mid-brown colour with slight mottling. Measured spec (average): metal 36, roughness 129, coat 116. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.

articles.title: Hardware: Cerakote Grey
articles.summary: Flat dark grey ceramic coat, fine sandy grain, almost no gloss, even matte surface with tiny sparkle. A gritty gunmetal grey with a salt-and-pepper mottle; from distance it is a flat dark olive-grey with a hint of texture.
articles.what: Ceramic in a polymer carrier, sprayed thin and baked — flatter than paint. Up close: Mottled grey-green granite-like grain: soft blobby speckle of light grey and near-black patches at about pea size, with a slightly greenish cast and larger smoky light and dark areas. High contrast within the grain, but no sharp edges. From a distance: A gritty gunmetal grey with a salt-and-pepper mottle; from distance it is a flat dark olive-grey with a hint of texture. Measured spec (average): metal 44, roughness 141, coat 124. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
